questions.question: An car moves through 20 m in 3 minutes and the next 50 km at a speed of 100 km/h. What is the approximate average speed of the car?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by the car to move 20 m = 3 minutes

Speed of the car for next 50 km = 100 km/h

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculation:**

Firstly, we will change m into km and minutes into hours.

⇒ 20 m = (20)/(1000)=0.02 km

⇒ 3 minutes = (3)/(60)=0.05 hours

Time taken by the car for remaining 50 km = (50)/(100)=0.5 hour

Average Speed of the car = (50+0.02)/(0.5+0.05)=(50.02)/(0.55)=90.94 km/h

Now, to convert the average speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by (5)/(18)

⇒ 90.94 km/h = 90.94times (5)/(18)=5.05 times 5=25.26 m/s

**Hence, the approximate average speed of the car is 25.26 m/s.**

questions.question: If the sum of the diagonals of a rhombus is L and the perimeter is 4P, find the area of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sum of diagonals of rhombus = L

Perimeter of rhombus = 4P

**Concept Used:**

Perimeter of Rhombus = 2sqrt{(Diagonal 1)²+(Diagonal 2)²}

Area of Rhombus = (1)/(2)times Product of Diagonals

**Calculation:**

Let the diagonals of the rhombus be d₁ and d₂

Perimeter of Rhombus = 4P

⇒ (4P)² = 4(d₁² + d₂²)

⇒ d12 + d₂² = (16P²)/(4)=4P²

As given,

Sum of diagonal, d₁ + d₂ = L

Squaring both sides,

⇒ (d₁ + d₂)² = L²

⇒ d₁² + d₂² + 2d₁d₂ = L²

⇒ 2d₁d₂ = L² – 4P²

⇒ d₁d₂ = (L²-4P²)/(2)

So, the Area of Rhombus = (1)/(2)times ((L²)/(2)-2P²) = (L²)/(4)-P² = (1)/(4) (L²-4P²) 

**Hence, the area of a rhombus is (1)/(4) (L²-4P²) .**

questions.question: If P = 7 × 4 - 3, Q = 8 ÷ 4 + 2, and R = 14 ÷ 21 × 9, then what is the value of P × Q + R?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P = 7 × 4 - 3

Q = 8 ÷ 4 + 2

R = 14 ÷ 21 × 9

**Concept Used:**

BODMAS = Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction

**Calculation:**

We have to find, P × Q + R

⇒ P × Q + R = (7times 4-3)times (8div 4+2)+(14÷21 times 9)

⇒ (28 – 3) × (2 + 2) + ((14)/(21)times 9)

⇒ 25 × 4 + 6 = 100 + 6 = 106

**Hence, the value of P × Q + R is 106.**

questions.question: The present ages of Vishal and Shekhar are in the ratio of 14 ∶ 17. Six years from now, their ages will be in the ratio of 17 ∶ 20. What is Shekhar's present age?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Present ages ratio of Vishal and Shekhar = 14 : 17

Ratio of ages after six years = 17 : 20

**Calculation:**

Let the present age of Vishal be 14x and Shekhar be 17x.

After six years,

Age of Vishal = 14x + 6

Age of Shekhar = 17x + 6

According to the question,

⇒ (14x+6)/(17x+6)=(17)/(20)

⇒ 20 × (14x + 6) = 17 × (17x + 6)

⇒ 280x + 120 = 289x + 102

⇒ 289x – 280x = 120 – 102

⇒ 9x = 18

⇒ x = (18)/(9) = 2

So, shekhar's present age = 17x = 17 × 2 = 34 years

**Hence, the present age of Shekhar is 34 years.**

questions.question: What is the difference between a discount of 35% and two successive discounts of 30% and 5% on a bill of ₹10,00,000?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Bill amount = Rs 10,00,000

Discount = 35%

Successive discounts = 30% and 5%

**Concept Used:**

Amount = Bill Amount – Discount

**Calculation:**

Amount after single discount = 1000000 – 35% of 1000000

Amount after single discount = 1000000-(35)/(100)× 1000000=1000000-350000=6,50,000 Rs

Amount after successive discount of 30% = 1000000 – 30% of 1000000

Amount after successive discount of 30% = 1000000-(30)/(100)× 1000000=7,00,000 Rs

Amount after a second successive discount of 5% = 700000 – 5% of 700000

Amount after a second successive discount of 5% = 700000-(5)/(100)× 700000=6,65,000 Rs

Difference between single and successive discounts = 665000 – 650000 = Rs 15,000

**Hence, the difference between a single discount and successive discount is of Rs 15,000**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Concept used:**

When two successive discounts X% and Y% are given,

Equivalent discount = (X + Y - XY/100)%

**Calculation:**

Amount after single discount of 35% = 1000000 - (35)/(100) × 1000000

= 1000000 - 350000

= Rs.650,000

Equivalent discount of two successive discount of 30% and 5% -

= [30 + 5 - (30 × 5)/100]

= 33.5%

Amount after equivalent discount = 1000000(1 - 33.5/100)

= 1000000 × 0.665

= Rs.665,000

∴ Difference between them = 665,000 - 650000 = Rs.15000

∴ **Required difference is Rs.15000.**

questions.question: The profit earned when a painting is sold for ₹1,200 is 15 times the loss incurred when it is sold for ₹240. At what price should be the painting be sold to make a profit of 40%?
questions.solution:

**Concept Used:**

Cost Price = SP + Loss

Selling Price = (100+Profit\%)/(100)times CP

**Calculation:**

Let the loss incurred when sold at ₹240 be ₹x.

So, Cost Price = 240 + x

Profit made when the painting sold at ₹1200 = 15x

Cost Price = 1200 – 15x

Then, 240 + x = 1200 – 15x

⇒ x + 15x = 1200 – 240 = 960

⇒ 16x = 960

⇒ x = 960 ÷ 16 = 60

Cost Price of painting = 240 + x = 240 + 60 = Rs.300

To make a profit of 40%,

Selling Price of the painting = (100+40)/(100)times 300=(140)/(100)times 300 = ₹420

**Hence, the painting should be sold at **₹**420 to make the profit of 40%.**

questions.question: The speed of a motor-boat in still water and the speed of the current of water are in the ratio 20 ∶ 4. To go a certain distance along the current the boat takes 4 hours. Find the time taken by the boat to cover the same distance against the current.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream Speed : Upstream Speed = (20 + 4) : (20 − 4) = 24 : 16 = 3 : 2

For a constant distance, time is inversely proportional to speed.

Time Downstream : Time Upstream = 2 : 3

Given Downstream Time (2 parts) = 4 hours, which means 1 part = 2 hours.

Upstream Time (3 parts) = 3 × 2 = 6 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the speed of the motor-boat in still water to the speed of the current = 20 : 4 = 5 : 1

Let the speed of the boat in still water be 5k and the speed of the current be k.

Time taken to cover a certain distance downstream = 4 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of current

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of current

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a511a63e0e00f62be742e085ebe19db7b55f1acdc0fc775ac452ba4647b967ae.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream Speed = 5k + k = 6k

⇒ Upstream Speed = 5k − k = 4k

⇒ Distance covered downstream = 6k × 4 = 24k

⇒ Since the boat covers the same distance, distance to be covered upstream = 24k

⇒ Time taken upstream = Distance ÷ Upstream Speed

⇒ Time taken upstream = 24k ÷ 4k = 6 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speed

If v is the speed of the boat in still water and u is the speed of the stream, then Downstream speed (D) = v + u and Upstream speed (U) = v − u.

Boat and Stream Speed Formula

When downstream speed (D) and upstream speed (U) are given, Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 and Speed of current = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed in Stream Journeys

When a boat travels from point A to point B downstream and immediately returns from point B to point A upstream, the average speed for the round trip is given by (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

questions.question: A man travels for 3 minutes at a speed of 22 km/h. What is the distance travelled by the man?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of man = 22 km/h

Time is taken to travel = 3 minutes

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

Firstly, convert km/h into m/s by multiplying by (5)/(18),

⇒ 22 km/h = 22times (5)/(18)=(55)/(9)

Now, 3 minutes = 180 seconds

Distance travelled by man = (55)/(9)times 180=55times 20=1100 metres

**Hence, the distance travelled by the man is 1100 metres.**

Value of A = 156-(25)/(100)times 156 = 156 - 39 = 117

questions.question: The average weight of A, B, C and D is 33 kg. C is 12 kg lighter than A, while B is 6 kg heavier than C. D's weight is 10 kg less than that of C. What is the average of A and D?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average weight of A, B, C, D = 33 kg

C is 12 kg lighter than A

B is 6 kg heavier than C

D is 10 kg less than that of C

**Concept Used:**

Average = Sum of values ÷ Number of values

**Calculation:**

Let the value of A be x kg.

Weight of C = x – 12 kg

Weight of B = x – 12 + 6 = x – 6 kg

Weight of D = x –12 – 10 = x – 22 kg

So, average of A, B, C and D = (x+x-12+x-6+x-22)/(4)=(4x-40)/(4) = x -10

⇒ x – 10 = 33

⇒ x = 33 + 10 = 43 kg

Then, Weight of A = 43 kg

Weight of D = x –22 = 43 – 22 = 21 kg

Average weight of A and D = (43+21)/(2)=(64)/(2) = 32 kg

**Hence, the average weight of A and D is 32 kg.**

questions.question: 22 boys, working together, can complete a work in 10 days, whereas 25 boys and 12 girls take 8 days to complete the same work. In how many days can only 6 girls, working together, complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of days taken by 22 boys to complete a work = 10 days

Number of days taken by 25 boys and 12 girls to complete the same work = 8 days

**Calculation:**

Let the one day work of 1 boy = x

Let the one day work of 1 girl = y

So, Total work done each day by 22 boys = 22x

⇒ 22x = (1)/(10)

⇒ x = (1)/(10× 22)=(1)/(220)

Now, According to the question for second condition,

⇒ 25x + 12y = (1)/(8)

Putting the value of x, we get

⇒ 25× (1)/(220)+12y=(1)/(8)

⇒ 12y = (1)/(8)-(5)/(44)

⇒ Taking LCM of the denominators,

⇒ 12y = (44-40)/(352)=(4)/(352)=(1)/(88)

⇒ y = (1)/(88× 12)

Number of days taken by 6 girls = 6y = 6× (1)/(88× 12)=(1)/(176) = 176 days

**Hence, the number of days taken by 6 girls, working together, to complete the work is 176 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let the efficiency of a boy = B

The efficiency of a girl = G

Then

Total work = 22 × 10 × B = (25 × B + 12 × G) × 8

20 × B = 96 × G

B/G = 24/5

B = 24 and G = 5

So total work = 22 × 10 × 24 

The efficiency of a girl = 5

So days required = 22 × 10 × 24/(5 × 6) = 22 × 8 = 176 days

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio of 1 ∶ 2 ∶ 3. The product of the three numbers is 1296. What is the sum of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of three numbers = 1 : 2 : 3

Product of three numbers = 1296

**Calculation:**

Let the numbers be x, 2x and 3x.

Product of three numbers = x × 2x × 3x = 6x³

⇒ 6x³ = 1296

⇒ x³ = (1296)/(6)=216

⇒ x = 6

So, First number = x = 6

Second Number = 2x = 2 × 6 = 12

Third Number = 3x = 3 × 6 = 18

Sum of all numbers = 6 + 12 + 18 = 36

**Hence, the sum of the three numbers is 36.**

questions.question: The area of a square is 1296 cm² and the radius of a circle is (7)/(6) of the length of a side of the square. What is the ratio of the perimeter of the square and the circumference of the circle? [Use π = (22)/(7)]
questions.solution:

Area of Square = 1296 cm²

Radius of circle = (7)/(6) of the length of a side of the square

**Concept Used:**

Area of Square = Side²

Perimeter of Square = 4 × Side

Circumference of Circle = 2pi r

**Calculation:**

Area of Square = Side² = 1296

Side = sqrt{1296} = 36 cm

Now, Radius of circle = (7)/(6)times 36 = 42 cm

Perimeter of Square = 4 × Side

Perimeter of Square = 4 × 36 = 144 cm

Circumference of circle = 2pi r

Circumference of circle = 2times (22)/(7)times 42=44times 6 = 264 cm

Ratio of Perimeter and Circumference = (144)/(264)=(6)/(11) = 6 : 11

**Hence, the ratio of the perimeter of square and circumference of circle is 6 : 11.**
